audit.whatIsWrong: Five rows contradict their own explanations. Row 0 says Zaahen while whys[0] calls it a skill check; row 2 says Skill while whys[2] says 'Level 3 stays yours'; row 4 says Zaahen while whys[4] says 'Level 6 is a wash'; rows 5 and 6 say Skill while whys[5] and whys[6] both describe Zaahen winning.
audit.why: The packet chart reads Skill / Zaahen / Zaahen / Skill / Skill / Zaahen / Zaahen and the mirror flipped exactly rows 0, 2, 4, 5 and 6 to match. That is 4 Zaahen / 3 Skill for a 51.89% lane over 3089 games.
audit.corrected: Flip rows 0, 2, 4, 5 and 6 in both layers, with ratings rescaled to 5/10, 6/10, 5/10, 6/10 and 6/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns anywhere, including on Hijack — which is the whole reason level 6 matters here.
audit.why: Chain Lash is 10s at rank 1, Kingslayer 12s, Abscond 13s, and Hijack is 80/55/30 — it drops to 30s at rank 3, so late in the game he is stealing an ultimate almost every fight. Zaahen's Q and E are 10s at rank 1, W 14s, R 110s.
audit.corrected: Number Chain Lash at 10s, Abscond at 13s, Kingslayer at 12s, and state that Hijack takes your R so Grim Deliverance is a finisher, never an opener.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three errors. (1) Chain Lash is written as (E) throughout the content layer — it is Q; Abscond/Abduct is E. (2) Kingslayer is called an 'execute' three times; Riot's text gives it no execute component at all — it is a 400-range lunge that damages and heals him against champions. (3) breakdown.cooldowns calls Abscond a 'dash + stun'; the recast Abduct pulls Sylas to an enemy, it does not stun. Zaahen's E is also called 'Golden Onslaught' rather than Aureate Rush.
audit.why: Riot's text for W: 'Sylas lunges at an enemy with magical force dealing damage and healing himself against enemy champions.' For E: 'Sylas dashes to a location. Sylas can recast the ability to throw his chains out, pulling himself to an enemy he hits.' The missing-interaction file flags needs-antiheal on Kingslayer — Grievous Wounds, not health thresholds, is what beats it, and the page told the player the opposite (stay healthy so the 'execute' never triggers).
audit.corrected: Fix the slot letters, replace the execute claim with the heal and the Grievous Wounds answer, and drop the phantom stun on Abscond.

edits.before: You own the early lane: Sylas is squishy and needs to land Chain Lash (E-Q double cast) to trade, so when his combo is down you walk up on Darkin Glaive (Q) and Golden Onslaught (E) and out-brawl him with Cultivation of War (P) healing. Punish him whenever he steps up to farm without E ready.
edits.after: You own the early lane: Sylas is squishy and needs Chain Lash (Q, 10s) to trade, so when it is down you walk up with The Darkin Glaive (Q) and Aureate Rush (E) and out-brawl him while Determination stacks. Punish every step he takes to farm without Abscond (E, 13s) ready.

edits.before: Sylas's Hijack (R) steals YOUR Final Retribution (R) or an ally ult, so respect the extra burst — but you're the bigger body, so if you engage before he can cleanly combo, your Q knock-up plus E outdamage his kit. Don't let him poke you to half with Kingslayer (W) heal before you commit.
edits.after: Hijack (R) steals YOUR ultimate, so hold Grim Deliverance until his is spent — at rank 1 his is 80s. You are the bigger body: engage before he combos and the Glaive recast knock-up plus Aureate Rush outdamage him. Don't let Kingslayer (W) poke-heal you to half first.

edits.before: You stay ahead — as a juggernaut your durability and P sustain beat his squishy poke once you close the gap, and his Kingslayer (W) execute only threatens you if you're already low. Keep the wave near you so his E-dash escape has no angle.
edits.after: You stay ahead — your durability and Determination stacks beat his squishy poke once you close, and Kingslayer (W, 12s) is a heal on a 400-range lunge, not an execute, so Grievous Wounds blunts it. Keep the wave near you so his E has no escape angle.

edits.before: You keep the sidelane 1v1: Sylas is a teamfight assassin, not a duelist, so isolate him and blow him up before Kingslayer (W) heals him. Mind his Hijack (R) in fights, but one-on-one your durability and Final Retribution (R) win.
edits.after: You keep the sidelane 1v1: Sylas is a teamfight assassin, not a duelist, so isolate him and burst through the Kingslayer (W) heal with Grievous Wounds. Mind Hijack (R) in fights — one-on-one your durability and Grim Deliverance win.

edits.after: Level 2 is yours — Sylas is squishy and combo-reliant, so when Chain Lash (Q, 10s) is down you step up with The Darkin Glaive and Aureate Rush and out-trade him while Determination stacks.

edits.after: Levels 3 through 6 stay in your favour: you out-brawl his poke whenever Chain Lash (Q) is on cooldown, and at 6 Hijack (R) steals your ultimate — so spend Grim Deliverance as a finisher, never an opener. Engage before he combos and the Q-E burst beats him.

notes: Third systematic slot swap in this slice: Chain Lash was written as (E) everywhere in the content layer. Also a fabricated mechanic — Kingslayer was described as an execute in three places and the player was advised to 'stay healthy so it never triggers'; Riot's text gives it no execute, only a heal, so the real answer is Grievous Wounds. And Abscond was described as a stun in breakdown.cooldowns; the recast is a pull. Five chart rows flipped as matched pairs with rescaled ratings.
